BRACKWATER BUILDING SOCIETY — COLLECTIONS & RECOVERIES
PAYMENT RELIEF POLICY PR-5 (EXTRACT), AMENDMENT PR-5/A1, AND APPLICATION FILE PRA-2026-02917

=== PAYMENT RELIEF POLICY PR-5 (VERSION 3, 1 FEBRUARY 2025) ===

1. Purpose
PR-5 sets the conditions under which Brackwater offers a temporary Payment Relief Plan (reduced monthly payments for up to six months, with the shortfall added to the balance) to residential mortgage customers in financial difficulty. Customers who do not qualify are still offered the standard arrears support options in policy PR-2 (payment arrangements, term extensions, referral to free debt advice). PR-5 decisions must be consistent and evidence-based; case handlers may not waive any eligibility condition.

2. Definitions
2.1 "Household" — the borrowers named on the mortgage and their spouses or partners living at the mortgaged property.
2.2 "Gross Monthly Income" — the total income of the Household before tax and deductions in a calendar month, including salary, wages, self-employed drawings, pensions and regular benefits. It excludes one-off payments: annual or discretionary bonuses, redundancy lump sums, gifts, inheritances, and tax refunds.
2.3 "Hardship Event" — a change of circumstances that reduces Household income, such as job loss, reduction of hours, illness, bereavement or relationship breakdown. The "Hardship Month" is the calendar month in which the Hardship Event occurred.
2.4 "Baseline Income" — the average Gross Monthly Income over the full calendar months immediately before the Hardship Month (the number of months is set in clause 3.1(a)).
2.5 "Current Income" — the average Gross Monthly Income over the two most recent full calendar months before the application date.
2.6 "Days Past Due" — the number of days since the oldest unpaid contractual monthly payment fell due, on the application date.
2.7 "Application date" — the date on which a complete application (form PR-5A plus evidence) is received.

3. Eligibility — all conditions must be met
3.1 (a) Qualifying hardship: Current Income is at least 25% lower than Baseline Income. Baseline Income is calculated over the 12 full calendar months before the Hardship Month.
    (b) Arrears: Days Past Due is 60 or fewer.
    (c) Frequency: no Payment Relief Plan has started in the 24 months before the application date. The 24 months are measured from the start date of the previous plan, not its end date.
    (d) Property: the mortgaged property is the Household's owner-occupied main residence. Buy-to-let and second homes are excluded.
    (e) Affordability: the reduced payment proposed by the customer is at least 50% of the contractual payment.
3.2 Where a condition is not met, the case handler records the condition and offers PR-2 options.

4. Plan terms
4.1 Maximum duration six months; review at month three.
4.2 Interest continues to accrue. The shortfall is capitalised at the end of the plan unless the customer repays it earlier.
4.3 Credit reporting: plans are reported as an "arrangement to pay" to credit reference agencies.

5. Evidence
5.1 Payslips or employer letters for each employed member of the Household covering the Baseline and Current periods; bank statements for the last three months; for self-employed customers, management accounts or bank statements.
5.2 Handlers must use gross figures from payslips. Net pay figures from bank statements are used only to check that the payslips are consistent.

6. Vulnerable customers
6.1 Customers showing signs of vulnerability are referred to the Specialist Support team, which may offer additional forbearance under policy PR-9. Referral does not change PR-5 eligibility.

7. Decisions and communication
7.1 Decisions are made within 10 business days of the application date. The customer receives a written decision explaining which conditions were met or not met.
7.2 Declined customers may ask for a review by a senior handler within 30 days; the review applies the same conditions.
7.3 Collection activity (letters, calls) is paused while an application is being assessed, but arrears continue to be reported.

8. Related policies (summary)
PR-2 Arrears support: payment arrangements of up to 12 months to clear arrears; temporary interest-only switch for up to 6 months; term extension subject to affordability; referral to free debt advice charities.
PR-9 Specialist support: additional flexibility for customers with serious illness, bereavement or domestic abuse, decided by the Specialist Support team.
PR-12 Litigation: the conditions under which Brackwater issues possession proceedings (never within 6 months of the first missed payment and never while an application under PR-5 or PR-9 is being assessed).

9. Record keeping
All calculations must be recorded in the case management system with the monthly figures used, so that the decision can be audited. Quality assurance samples 10% of decisions each month.

=== AMENDMENT PR-5/A1 (EFFECTIVE 1 JULY 2026, FOR APPLICATIONS RECEIVED FROM THAT DATE) ===
(1) In clause 3.1(a), "12 full calendar months" is replaced by "6 full calendar months".
(2) The 25% threshold and the definition of Gross Monthly Income (including the exclusion of one-off payments) are unchanged.
(3) New clause 3.1(f): customers with an active County Court claim must be referred to Litigation before a plan is offered. [Not applicable in this file — no claim issued.]

=== APPLICATION FILE PRA-2026-02917 ===
Borrowers: Mr Callum Deverell and Ms Anya Deverell (joint mortgage).
Property: 19 Heron Walk, Brackwater — owner-occupied main residence since 2018.
Mortgage balance: GBP 213,400. Product: 5-year fixed rate 4.19% until 31 May 2028, early repayment charge 3%. Remaining term: 21 years 4 months. Loan-to-value: 61% (desktop valuation, January 2026). Contractual monthly payment: GBP 1,286.
Application date: 10 September 2026 (form PR-5A and full evidence received).
Proposed reduced payment: GBP 700 per month for six months.

Hardship Event: Ms Deverell's employer reduced her contract from 37.5 to 22.5 hours per week with effect from 1 March 2026 (employer letter dated 12 February 2026). Hardship Month: March 2026.

Household gross income (from payslips), by month:
- September 2025: GBP 6,200
- October 2025: GBP 6,200
- November 2025: GBP 6,200
- December 2025: GBP 9,200 (includes Mr Deverell's annual performance bonus of GBP 3,000, shown separately on the payslip as "Annual bonus")
- January 2026: GBP 6,200
- February 2026: GBP 6,200
- March 2026: GBP 5,050
- April 2026: GBP 4,960
- May 2026: GBP 4,900
- June 2026: GBP 4,850
- July 2026: GBP 4,780
- August 2026: GBP 4,760

Household net pay received in bank account (for consistency check only): September 2025 – February 2026 average GBP 4,650 (excluding December bonus); July–August 2026 average GBP 3,390.

Arrears: payments due 15 July 2026 and 15 August 2026 missed; the 15 July payment is the oldest unpaid payment. Days Past Due on 10 September 2026: 57.

Other commitments (from credit file): car finance GBP 289 per month; two credit cards with total balance GBP 3,120, minimum payments up to date. No County Court judgments.
Vulnerability screening: no indicators recorded; customer declined referral to debt advice for now.
Previous forbearance: Payment Relief Plan PRP-2024-0551, started 1 June 2024, ended 30 November 2024; completed successfully.

Customer's covering letter: "Our take-home pay has dropped by more than a quarter — from about £4,650 a month to about £3,390. We are behind by two payments and want to get back on track. We had a plan in 2024 but that ended almost two years ago."

Handler's draft calculation (first line, 11 September 2026):
"Baseline (Sep–Feb, 6 months): total 40,200 / 6 = 6,700. Current (Jul–Aug): 4,770. Drop = 28.8% — over 25%. Net drop 27.1% also over 25%. DPD 57 (OK). Previous plan started June 2024 — more than 24 months ago (OK). Owner-occupied (OK). Proposed 700 is 54% of 1,286 (OK). Recommend approve."
Team leader note: "Please double-check the income definitions before approval."

state.setting: A fantasy village in a video game. The player speaks out loud and a speech-to-text system transcribes it. The characters listed are the non-player characters within earshot.
state.transcript_quality: Raw speech-to-text output: lowercase, no punctuation, and names may be spelled the way they sound.

instructions.question: Is the player speaking to Jeff, the guard?
instructions.speaking_to_means: Jeff is an intended listener who should pay attention or respond. That includes being addressed by name, nickname, role, or description; being the character the player faces when saying 'you'; being part of a group the player addresses; or being the natural continuation of an ongoing conversation with Jeff.
instructions.not_speaking_to: Jeff is merely the topic, a third party the player talks about, someone the player asks another character to relay a message to, or a name that only appears inside quoted speech.

criteria.true: Jeff is an intended listener of this utterance.
criteria.false: Jeff is not being spoken to.
